g.title: MaleHypogonadism_QSP
g.text: HPG axis · SHBG binding equilibrium · intratesticular testosterone · erythropoiesis · bone · body composition · 7 testosterone formulations + 5 non-androgen strategies

g.title: cluster_hypo
g.text: ① Hypothalamus — GnRH pulse generator (KNDy neurons)

g.title: cluster_sertoli
g.text: ④ Testis — Sertoli cells and spermatogenesis (74-day cycle + epididymal transit)

g.title: cluster_bind
g.text: ⑤ Circulating binding equilibrium — the mathematical centre of this map (Vermeulen mass action)

g.title: cluster_shbg
g.text: ⑥ SHBG regulation — disease, treatment and ageing push it opposite ways

g.title: cluster_metab
g.text: ⑦ Peripheral metabolism — one hormone splits three ways

g.title: cluster_sec
g.text: ⑩ Secondary (central) hypogonadism — LH/FSH normal or ↓

g.title: cluster_func
g.text: ⑪ Functional hypogonadism — the self-reinforcing obesity · inflammation loop (reversible)

g.title: cluster_ery
g.text: ⑫ Erythropoiesis — mechanism of the commonest TRT adverse event (the second convexity)

g.title: cluster_bone
g.text: ⑬ Bone — the effect runs mostly through E2, not T

g.title: cluster_body
g.text: ⑭ Muscle · body composition — the most clearly dose-dependent endpoints

g.title: cluster_cns
g.text: ⑮ Central nervous system — libido · erection · mood · cognition

g.title: cluster_cv
g.text: ⑰ Cardiovascular · safety — the landscape after TRAVERSE

g.title: cluster_pk
g.text: ⑱ Testosterone formulation PK — same weekly dose, different waveform

g.title: cluster_alt
g.text: ⑲ Non-androgen strategies — raising T without switching the axis off (fertility preserved)

g.title: cluster_supp
g.text: ⑳ Axis shutdown by exogenous androgen — the pathophysiology treatment creates

g.title: cluster_dx
g.text: ㉑ Diagnosis · monitoring — the problem that the threshold depends on SHBG

g.title: cluster_end
g.text: ㉒ Clinical endpoints and key trials (model calibration targets)

g.title: LHCGR
g.text: shared Gs — hCG t½ far longer

g.title: STAR
g.text: rate-limiting step: cholesterol import into mitochondria

g.title: T_ALB
g.text: K_A ≈ 3.6×10⁴ M⁻¹ · low affinity · high capacity

g.title: EPO_K
g.text: T → upward shift of the oxygen set point

g.title: SUPP_LH
g.text: LH suppression (below assay limit within days)

g.title: CONVEX
g.text: ⇒ FT is a convex function of TT

g.title: HEP_CL
g.text: acts on the bioavailable fraction only

g.title: MISCLASS
g.text: low SHBG: TT is low but FT is normal
high SHBG: TT is normal but FT is low
⇒ a single TT threshold is wrong in both directions

g.title: VERM
g.text: a = N·K_S, b = N + K_S·S − K_S·T

g.title: JENSEN
g.text: at the same mean TT a higher-amplitude regimen

g.title: CONVEX2
g.text: ⚑ The second convexity does not compose
the erythroid response is convex only in its lower limb
and supraphysiologic peaks cross into Hill's concave upper limb
⇒ model result: peak gain ≈ 0 or negative
(the point that refuted the hypothesis — reported, not hidden)

g.title: HNF4A
g.text: master regulator of the SHBG promoter

g.title: OPP
g.text: treating obesity raises TT and lowers SHBG at once
⇒ FT rises further than TT does

g.title: CAG
g.text: shorter → higher transcriptional activity — varies between subjects

g.title: CHEMO
g.text: loss of Leydig and spermatogonial cells

g.title: SEC_LAB
g.text: Laboratory picture: TT ↓, LH normal/↓, FSH normal/↓

g.title: OSA_F
g.text: sleep fragmentation → loss of nocturnal LH pulses

g.title: FPN
g.text: hepcidin ↓ → more retained at the membrane

g.title: THRESH
g.text: ⚑ What manufactures the gap is the decision rule
applying a fixed Hct>54% threshold to a population distribution
turns a ~1-point mean shift into a ~2.5-fold difference in incidence
⇒ a property of the stopping rule, not of the molecule

g.title: PHLEB
g.text: Therapeutic phlebotomy / dose reduction / change of formulation

g.title: FX_RISK
g.text: increased instead in the TRT arm (HR 1.43)

g.title: FALLS
g.text: Change in activity level and fall exposure

g.title: FINK
g.text: body fat = E2-dependent (rises under aromatase inhibition)

g.title: FINK_T
g.text: dissociation of the T vs E2 contributions

g.title: LIBIDO
g.text: depends on both T and E2 · continuous in dose

g.title: TTRIAL_V
g.text: T-Trials vitality/walking: primary endpoint not met

g.title: SLEEP_CNS
g.text: Sleep quality / possible worsening of OSA

g.title: PSA
g.text: +0.3-0.5 ng/mL in the first 6 months of TRT

g.title: PCA_RISK
g.text: no signal of increase in meta-analyses or TRAVERSE

g.title: SATUR
g.text: AR is saturated above ~TT 250 ng/dL, so

g.title: BP_T
g.text: Blood pressure — raised on oral TU (boxed warning)

g.title: PLAQUE
g.text: increased in the T-Trials CV substudy

g.title: WAVEFORM
g.text: doubling the amplitude at the same weekly dose
changes Hct by only ~0.1 points (model result)
most of the gap between formulations is a dose difference

g.title: TU_PO
g.text: lymphatic uptake · fat-meal dependent · high peaks

g.title: GEL_TD
g.text: near steady state · small diurnal swing

g.title: PELLET
g.text: 6-12 pellets q3-6 months · near zero-order release

g.title: WAVEFORM->HCT_INC
g.text: what the formulation gap has to explain

g.title: FERT_NOTE
g.text: If fertility is the goal, the LH signal must not be switched off.

g.title: ANAST
g.text: ⚠ at the cost of bone loss

g.title: SYMPT
g.text: (low libido · loss of morning erections · gynaecomastia)

g.title: LEG1
g.text: Black arrow = activation/flow Red arrow = inhibition Green arrow = therapeutic intervention

g.title: LEG2
g.text: ⚑ marked = the quantitative core claim of this model (computed by the analysis functions of the mrgsolve model)

g.title: LEG3
g.text: Pink notes = convexity · Jensen · misclassification — one connected argument
